pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome from the Chair of Governors - St. James' Catholic High School
pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Chair of Governors
On behalf of the Governing Body I would like to warmly welcome you to St James' Catholic High School.
Our school was founded by the Dominican Sisters in 1934 to provide Catholic secondary education for children in the parishes of north-west London. Today, the school maintains its Dominican traditions and continues its role in the mission of the Church. Our gospel values and the principles of respect and consideration are fundamental to everything that we do.
The Governors are justly proud of our school's tradition of achievement, its excellent reputation for Catholic education and pastoral care. We believe our school offers an outstanding environment in which all students can thrive.
We have extremely high expectations of both staff and pupils here at St James' and under the outstanding guidance of our Senior Leadership Team and all the staff, we will do our utmost to ensure that every pupil reaches their full potential, both academically as well as growing spiritually in their Catholic faith.
You will have seen the excellent results achieved by our pupils this year and we look forward to enjoying continued success in the future. I believe your child will enjoy every aspect of their time at St James' Catholic High School and will be a valued member of our school community.

pageCache.pageTitle: Mission, Vision and Values - St. James' Catholic High School
pageCache.text:
Mission, Vision and Values
At St James’, everything we do is underpinned by our mission statement from the Gospel of John:
“I have come that they may have life and have it to the full” – John 10:10
To give every child, regardless of background, starting points or ability, the opportunity to live life to the full.
For our pupils to finish their secondary education at St James', ready and equipped to progress into the next chapter of their lives. That they will have a strong personal vision for adult life, a commitment to the communities they will serve and champions of the Gospel and our Veritas Values
Our VERITAS values of Excellence, Resilience, Integrity, Trust, Aspiration and Service are instilled in our pupils, providing the foundations for our pupils to succeed in that vision.

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome from the Headteacher - St. James' Catholic High School
pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Headteacher
As Headteacher it is my great privilege to be leading a school where the holistic development of our pupils, as set out in our mission statement, is our core purpose.
Our mission statement: ‘I have come that they may have life and have it to the full’ ~ John 10:10
Our commitment to the pursuit of academic excellence and our rich personal development curriculum is underpinned by our Catholic identity, brought to life through our Veritas Values.
Our curriculum is broad and well balanced, designed and delivered by expert teachers to support all pupils to reach and exceed their academic potential. This is in conjunction with a bespoke Personal Health, Social and Citizenship Education (PHSCE) programme and a wide ranging extra-curricular offer that is outstanding.
It is our intention that this, supported by our ethos and values, will allow each pupil to complete a seven year journey with us and take their place in society where their gifts and talents will be of benefit to all.
We insist on the highest standards of behaviour for learning and have clear policies in place to ensure these are maintained. It is my absolute belief that this consistency of approach enables our community to flourish and enables our pupils to live out our mission statement.
Thank you for taking the time to visit our website, if you have any questions, please do get in touch with us by completing the form below.
“St James’ Catholic High School is a caring and inclusive school.”
“The school’s ‘Veritas values’ and its house system encourage pupils and sixth-form students to take on additional responsibility within the school and community."
“The partnership between parents, school and parish is outstanding.”
“Human flourishing is at the heart of the school’s Mission Statement which reinforces the school’s aspiration for every pupil to reach his or her God given potential.”
Diocese of Westminster 2019

pageCache.pageTitle: Faith in Action - St. James' Catholic High School
pageCache.text:
Faith in Action
Our Charities
At St. James' Catholic School, charity is much more than fundraising—it is a way of living out our faith. Guided by the Dominican Pillars of Prayer, Study, Community, and Service, we encourage every member of our school family to recognise the dignity of every person and respond with compassion and generosity. Through prayer, we remember those in need; through study, we deepen our understanding of the causes of poverty and injustice; through community, we work together to support one another; and through service, we put our faith into action by supporting local, national, and international charities.
Each year group at St. James' proudly supports a chosen charity throughout the academic year, planning and participating in a range of fundraising activities and awareness campaigns. This gives every pupil the opportunity to make a meaningful contribution to causes that reflect our Catholic values while developing a deeper understanding of the challenges faced by others. Inspired by Catholic Social Teaching, particularly the principles of human dignity, the common good, solidarity, and the preferential option for the poor, our pupils are empowered to become active citizens who make a positive difference in the world.
At St. James', we are committed to developing young people who lead with faith, serve with compassion, and strive to build a more just and caring society, reflecting Christ's love in all that they do.
Scrub-up Hub
The Scrub-Up-Hub grew out of our Jubilee Year of Hope, when students identified hygiene poverty as an issue they wanted to address within their own community. They organised a whole-school giving drive, asking different year groups to donate everyday hygiene essentials including shampoo, toothpaste, deodorant, soap, washing products and sanitary items. With generous additional support from our Dominican Associates, students created the Scrub-Up-Hub: a cupboard of toiletries and household hygiene products available to any student who needs something for themselves or their family. Dignity has been central to the initiative from the beginning, so the Hub is particularly accessible at the end of the school day, allowing students to take what they need quietly and discreetly. It is a wonderful example of our young people recognising a need and putting hope, compassion and service into action.
Emergency Foodbank
In partnership with our local parishes and generous members of staff, we keep a selection of emergency food items available for students and families to access whenever they are needed. We are particularly grateful to the Parish of St Margaret Clitherow, who regularly provide breakfast bars and other quick, nutritious items for students who may have missed breakfast because of a difficult morning or challenging family or financial circumstances. We are also very grateful to the Parish of the Annunciation, whose generous donations provide a wider range of food items for our emergency supplies. This quiet, practical support enables us to respond with care and dignity when members of our community need a little extra help.
Second-hand Uniform
Each summer, we hold a second-hand uniform sale, providing families with the opportunity to purchase good-quality uniform at a greatly reduced cost. This can be particularly helpful for families joining St James’, when purchasing a complete new school uniform all at once can be a significant expense. We also keep a supply of second-hand uniform in school throughout the year so that we can offer practical and discreet support to families experiencing challenging circumstances.
Our Sixth Form students have also coordinated a second-hand business-wear swap, inviting staff and Year 13 students to donate good-quality clothing to support students entering the Sixth Form with the smart business wear they need.
By passing on uniform that still has plenty of life left in it, we are also reducing waste and putting our commitment to care for our community and our common home into practice.

pageCache.pageTitle: Prayer - St. James' Catholic High School
pageCache.text:
Prayer
Prayer is at the heart of life in our Dominican school. Rooted in the Dominican tradition, we believe that prayer is the foundation of our relationship with God and the source of the wisdom, compassion, and courage needed to live out the Gospel each day. Through personal reflection, shared worship, and the celebration of the Church's liturgy, prayer invites us to encounter Christ, discern His presence in our lives, and grow in faith together.
As a community inspired by the Dominican Pillars of Prayer, Study, Community, and Service, we recognise that prayer not only strengthens our relationship with God but also inspires us to seek truth (Veritas), care for one another, and put our faith into action. Prayer calls us to reflect on the needs of others and to respond with compassion, justice, and hope.
Our life of prayer is closely connected to the principles of Catholic Social Teaching. Through prayer, we deepen our understanding of the dignity of every human person, our responsibility to work for the common good, our call to stand in solidarity with those who are vulnerable, and our duty to be good stewards of God's creation. Prayer challenges us not only to reflect on these values but also to live them out through acts of service, advocacy, and love. In this way, prayer becomes both a source of spiritual nourishment and a catalyst for positive action, enabling our whole school community to be faithful witnesses to the Gospel in everyday life.

pageCache.pageTitle: Catholic Social Teaching - St. James' Catholic High School
pageCache.text:
Catholic Social Teaching
At St James’, we are passionate about Catholic Social Teaching because we understand the important role it plays in forming our young people to become the fullest versions of themselves and to recognise the part they can play in building a better world.
Our vision is that every young person leaves St James’ able and willing to help bring about the Kingdom of God here on Earth - a Kingdom of peace, justice, love and joy.
Catholic Social Teaching helps us to understand what that looks like in practice. It begins with the dignity of every human person: the understanding that every individual is made in the image and likeness of God and is therefore of infinite worth. From this flows our responsibility to participate in society and work for the common good; to stand alongside those experiencing injustice or suffering; to put the needs of the poor and vulnerable first, rather than at the back of the queue; and to care for the gifts entrusted to us - our own gifts and talents, the gifts of others, and our common home.
At St James’, Catholic Social Teaching is something we learn, but more importantly something we seek to live.
It can be found across our curriculum as students are encouraged to consider questions of dignity, justice, responsibility and the common good through different subjects. But it is also woven into the everyday life and culture of our school.
We live it through our restorative approach to relationships; our charitable giving and social action; our Student Council and the opportunities students have to participate and make their voices heard; our commitment to inclusion, diversity and anti-bullying; our Gardening Club and care for creation; and the practical support we offer members of our community when times are difficult.
It is reflected in our determination to ensure that disadvantage does not become a barrier to opportunity, and in the choices we make to give particular support and access to those who may otherwise have less. Most fundamentally, it is present in our commitment to creating a school in which every young person is known, seen and valued.
Catholic Social Teaching challenges us to look beyond ourselves and ask not simply “What do I want?” but “What is my responsibility to others?” “Whose voice is not being heard?” “Who needs me to stand alongside them?” and “How can I use what I have been given for the good of others?”
In this way, we hope to form young people who not only understand the principles of Catholic Social Teaching, but have developed the habits, compassion and courage to live them - using their gifts to become people of peace, justice, love and joy in whatever communities they go on to serve.

pageCache.pageTitle: Subjects - St. James' Catholic High School
pageCache.text:
Subjects
Here you will find an overview of each of the subjects that students study here at St James'.
These overviews lay out the major topics your child will cover each term. It will also show you the key marked tasks that our staff and pupils will be focussing on.
Our curriculum has been carefully designed to take into account the starting points of all learners and the requirements of external examinations.
You can help by asking your child to tell you more about these topics and ask to see the feedback on their formative assessment.(what the teacher marks to gauge their understanding)
Art
Art makes students look at things in new ways– even mundane ordinary aspects of the world. There is something magical about expressing ideas or emotions with pencil and paint or sculpting with your hands. Communicating with colour, shape and form awakens the imagination; it opens doors to better understanding of humankind.
subject curriculum OVERVIEW
Business and Economics
Students will gain an appreciation that businesses are a key part of the world around us. Most students will eventually either work for a business organisation or run a business. Business and work related skills are therefore essential to fulfilling potential and having life to the full. The actions of a business can have an impact on the environment and communities, so it is important businesses consider their ethical and social responsibility.
Subject curriculum overview
Computing
Our Computing Department aims to equip students with essential computer literacy skills, fostering their ability to understand and use hardware, software, and broader technology effectively. We focus on building a foundation in problem-solving, digital citizenship, and developing skills across various forms of software. Through engaging lessons and the integration of both theory and practice, we nurture learning and creativity at every stage. Across our courses, our curriculum covers key areas such as data representation, programming, cyber security, and graphics, in order to prepare students for academic, social, and professional success in the modern digital world.
Subject Curriculum Overview
Drama
The Drama Department aims to stimulate a lifelong curiosity, interest and enjoyment in drama and dramatic literature from a variety of cultures and traditions. Our young people develop a range of personal qualities, including perseverance, resilience, initiative, confidence, individual awareness and group sensitivity. We want students to develop their drama skills and enjoy a range of performance opportunities especially in our new theatre space. Students here are helped to aspire to professional standards in a professional environment. We aim to offer a diverse and original programme of teaching and learning activities which develop confidence, mastery and a sense of pride.
Subject Curriculum Overview
Design Technology
Our D&T curriculum is aimed at equipping students with a range of design skills. Students explore a range of objects, how certain working parts are made and how to join, fix and use materials effectively. They learn to assemble, disassemble, plan, construct and evaluate projects.
Subject Curriculum Overview
English
Here at St James', we believe that the purpose of the study of English is the pursuit of truth through interpretation. This pursuit of truth places our VERITAS values at the heart of our mission that pupils may 'have life and have it to the full'. We see truth (which encompasses morality, knowledge and the human experience and condition) as being relative to context and therefore it is vital for pupils to have a wide knowledge and understanding of the world in order to interpret texts meaningfully. We seek to develop students' conceptual understanding of English and to teach them the core knowledge that will enable them to continue studying until KS5.
Subject Curriculum Overview
Food Technology
At St James' FT aims to inspire and to develop healthy, independent and capable cooks who are able to understand the food commodities, nutrients and cookery skills that will enable them to live life to the full.
Subject curriculum overview
Geography
We believe that to be a successful geographer it is important to approach the discipline through the threshold concepts , which we have identified as:
Subject Curriculum Overview
A world which is under dispute.
A world which is increasingly globalised.
A world which is unequal.
History
At St James' History aims to develop a deep understanding of developments, trends and patterns. With the skills and conceptual understanding acquired through the study of History, students will be able to navigate the present.
subject curriculum OVERVIEW
Maths
Mathematics is not simply numbers, equations or algorithms. It is about understanding the world. Dive down deep enough into ANYTHING and you will find Mathematics. I feel honoured to be able to empower, educate, and enhance our amazing students.'Education is the passport to the future, for tomorrow belongs to those who prepare for it today' - Malcolm X
Subject Curriculum Overview
MFL
The KS3 curriculum sets out to gradually improve our students’ knowledge and skills in order to provide a solid base for transition to GCSE. It has been designed to give every student the opportunity to understand that success is achievable regardless of ability or starting point.
Subject Curriculum Overview
Media
The creative media sector is an exciting, dynamic, growing and rewarding sector to work in. In this BTEC tech award you will learn to develop a wide range of skills and techniques from broadcast media to interactive platforms. This qualification helps students to explore the media sector by undertaking practical media projects. During the course students will:
This qualification is the same size and level as a GCSE aimed at those interested in pursuing a career in creative media production.
Subject Curriculum Overview
Develop digital media production skills and techniques
Music
At St James' Music aims to arm our students with the tools necessary to communicate their own emotions through music, giving them the opportunity to pursue their own truth through expression. We see music as an art form and a cultural activity, whose medium is vocal or instrumental sounds combined in such a way as to produce beauty of form, harmony, and expression of emotion.
Subject Curriculum Overview
PE
The PE Department is a thriving and busy department with an excellent reputation. There is a passion for sport and we pride ourselves on our enthusiasm and commitment to getting students involved and trying to discover that little bit of brilliance in all of them. The PE department delivers a challenging yet enjoyable curriculum across a wide range of sports. There are also numerous sporting opportunities available after and during school where students can attend one of the team practices or attend clubs for enjoyment.
Subject Curriculum Overview
PSHCE
PSHCE at St James' remains responsive to what knowledge and support students need for their unique challenges and contexts, allowing them to live life to the full both during their time here and beyond. We welcome input from students and parents and therefore will be seeking your views throughout the course of the academic year.
RE
Our Catholic curriculum provides the framework for our students’ understanding of British values. In the RE classroom, lessons draw on the example of Jesus and His welcome and inclusion of all, especially those who were on the periphery of society. This is also developed in Catholic Social Teaching. The RE classroom must be a democratic classroom where all pupils have an equal right to be heard and democracy is modelled by the teacher and expected of every pupil.
Subject Curriculum Overview
Social Science
At St James' the social sciences aim to prepare all students to view the world more critically by understanding an array of factors that can determine our behaviour, whether this be biological or learnt processes or society. We investigate a variety of approaches and use evidence to understand which explanation best explains why we are the way we are.
Subject Curriculum Overview
Subject Curriculum Overview
Health & Social Care:
Subject Curriculum Overview
Science
Science at St James is aimed to develop and encourage a 'can do' mindset in learners by ensuring that the curriculum is relevant and accessible to all. We provide the appropriate stretch and challenge at every stage. Through building up a body of key foundational knowledge and concepts, we encourage students to recognise the power of rational explanations and develop a sense of excitement and curiosity about natural phenomena. Students are taught to understand how science is used to explain what is occurring, predict how things will behave, analyse causes, encourage creativity and problem solve.

Investors in People Accreditation for St James'
PRESS RELEASE FROM INVESTORS in PEOPLE
Investors in People is delighted to award St James’ Catholic High School with the “We Invest in People” accreditation.
It means principles and practices around supporting people are in place and everyone understands how to use them to make work better!
St James’ is committed to providing fantastic opportunities for all of the school community, whether it be pupils or staff.
Paul Devoy, CEO of Investors in People, said: “We’d like to congratulate St James’ Catholic High School. Being accredited with We invest in people is a remarkable effort for any organisation, and places St James’] in fine company with a host of organisations that understand the value of people.”
Commenting on the award, Headteacher Mr Ellul said: “We’re delighted with this recognition of St James’ as an employer that supports it’s staff. We are committed to work on this going forward and ensure that we are an even better place to work. We believe that the success of our school begins and ends with people.“

pageCache.pageTitle: Celebrating GCSE Success at St James’ - Celebrating GCSE Success at St James’ - News Blog - St. James' Catholic High School
pageCache.text:
Celebrating GCSE Success at St Jamesâ
There were plenty of smiles across St James’ as our Year 11 pupils opened their GCSE results and celebrated the culmination of years of hard work, determination and resilience.
We are incredibly proud to share another great set of GCSE results, building on the successes of previous years, with pupils achieving strong outcomes across a wide range of subjects.
A Fantastic Year of Achievement
Our pupils have achieved some excellent results this year, with:
These results are a fantastic reflection of the commitment shown by our pupils throughout their GCSE journey.
Headteacher Anthony Ellul said:
“We are so proud of our pupils. They are a credit to our school, and we couldn’t be happier to see the smiles as they opened up their results today. Throughout their time with us, they have lived out our VERITAS values, and I can’t wait to see how this translates to a positive impact on the wider world.”
There were some particularly impressive performances across individual subjects.
Celebrating Our Pupils
Huge congratulations to the students who have all achieved a GCSE grade average of 8 or above:
Amelie Marks, Filip Apopei , Emilia Chmiel , Joseph McDonnell, Beryl Lam, Karolina Tomaszewska, Elirton Gjoni , Justin Ioan, Janice Ng, Sangala Okuku, Moses Urang, Tommy Cooke, Arianna Mok, Andreea Ursachi and Edmond Owusu. Further congratulations to Edmond who achieved highest Business Studies mark in the whole of the country!
These achievements represent just a small selection of the fantastic results achieved by our Year 11 pupils.
Head of Year 11, Jacques Vercuiel, said,:
"Our Year 11 pupils have shown tremendous perseverance and maturity throughout their GCSE journey. They embraced every opportunity to succeed, and these results are a fitting reward for their hard work. We are incredibly grateful to our staff and parents for the encouragement they have given, and we look forward to welcoming many of our pupils into the Sixth Form."
Looking Ahead to Sixth Form
For many of our pupils, results day marks the beginning of the next chapter of their St James’ journey, with a large number preparing to return to our Sixth Form in September.
“I’m really happy with my results and so proud of what I have achieved. All the hard work and revision has paid off, and it feels amazing to see the results today. I’m really grateful to the teachers for all their support and encouragement throughout the year.”
“I’m so pleased with my results and couldn’t be happier with how everything has turned out!”
“I am absolutely delighted with my GCSE results. I was really nervous coming in this morning, so seeing my grades was such a great feeling. I am really proud of myself and thankful to everyone at the school who helped me along the way.”
We would like to congratulate every member of our Year 11 cohort on their achievements. We are incredibly proud of the hard work, resilience and determination they have shown, and we look forward to seeing all they go on to achieve.

pageCache.text:
PSHE Curriculum
Our PSHE curriculum is founded on several pillars. If you are interested in learning more about our programme, please email admin@st-james.barnet.sch.uk for the attention of Mr Joe Langtry (Head of PSHE). Catholic Church and Diocese of Westminster – We are a Catholic School and fully support the teachings of the Catholic Church and guidance provided by the Diocese of Westminster.
PSHE Association – We are a member of the PSHE Association - the leading national body for PSHE guidance, training and guidance.
Staff Voice – Our staff give feedback on PSHE lessons and wider trends around the school, both from a pastoral and social perspective. This ensures our PSHE offering is up to date with school trends.
Student Voice – Pupil feedback is passed from the student body through the House Council. Pupils are encouraged to offer their thoughts, particularly through inspiration on what captures attention and interest through what they see, hear and read about on social media. Recent examples include the inclusion of first aid lessons for Year 12 pupils provided by the Red Cross and a suite of Year 8 lessons about safety on social media.

Careers Advice
We offer one-to-one careers advice to students across the school. This support is provided by our external careers guidance partner, Seetec.
Message from Seetec:
Seetec is an employee-owned organisation that delivers services to support people into work, develop skills, and create positive change within the communities we serve. We have over 40 years’ experience delivering high-quality services across employability, skills, careers guidance, apprenticeships, and rehabilitation.
Seetec has been supporting students at St James since September 2025. We provide one-to-one careers guidance meetings to help students explore their options and make informed decisions about their future pathways.
Careers Adviser Contact Details: Name: Cem Mustafa Email: cmustafa@st-james.barnet.sch.uk
